# Track & Trace ontology tutorial shortcut: Set up parts 0 to 2 with one notebook

Use this page instead of the setup steps of [part 0](tutorial-0-introduction.md) and, if you want, instead of
[part 1](tutorial-1-create-ontology.md) and [part 2](tutorial-2-enrich-ontology.md). One notebook creates the
lakehouse, the eventhouse and the semantic model of part 0, loads the sample data into them, and then creates the
ontology of parts 1 and 2. You add the three entity types that it can't create, and continue with
[part 3](tutorial-3-explore-ontology.md).

The notebook runs in your Fabric workspace as you. It uses your Fabric sign-in for every call, so you don't need
keys, passwords, an app registration or a connection. It downloads the sample data from this repository on GitHub,
which is public.

Use it to set up a demo tenant quickly, or to rebuild the environment before a rehearsal. Read part 0 first anyway:
its first sections explain what the demo must show and why.

## What the notebook creates

| Tutorial step | Item | What's in it |
|---|---|---|
| Part 0, Prepare the lakehouse | Lakehouse **TrackTraceLH**, with lakehouse schemas | The CSV files under **Files** (the `pack` part files under **Files/pack**), and 18 tables under **Tables > dbo** with 182,829 rows |
| Part 0, Prepare the eventhouse | Eventhouse **TrackTraceEH** with its KQL database **TrackTraceEH** | The tables **TraceEvent** (182,893 rows) and **LineScannerTelemetry** (20,736 rows) |
| Part 0, Create the semantic model | Semantic model **TrackTraceKPIs** | The same model as `notebooks/create_semantic_model.ipynb` creates |
| Parts 1 and 2 | Ontology **TrackTraceOntology** | The same ontology as [the shortcut for parts 1 and 2](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md) creates: 22 entity types (18 if your tenant doesn't accept the inherited ones through the API), 24 relationship types and 6 rules |

It doesn't create the following:

- Trace Event, Scanner Telemetry and Line Production Day, and their relationship types. You add them in the ontology editor in about 10 minutes,
  as described in [Finish the ontology in the editor](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#finish-the-ontology-in-the-editor).
- Anything in Microsoft 365 or Copilot Studio: the work context, the mock incident list and the agents of
  [part 5](tutorial-5-build-demo-agents.md).

## Prerequisites

- A workspace on a Fabric capacity (an F SKU or a trial). Eventhouses and ontology items need a Fabric capacity.
- The tenant settings of part 0: **Users can create ontology (preview) items** and **Users can create Fabric items**.
- The contributor role or higher in the workspace.
- Notebooks in the workspace can reach `raw.githubusercontent.com`. If your workspace blocks outbound access, see
  [If the notebook can't reach GitHub](#if-the-notebook-cant-reach-github).

You don't need to download the sample data first. You only need the notebook file: on GitHub, open
`notebooks/setup_workspace.ipynb` in the `pmi-track-and-trace-ontology` branch, and select **Download raw file**.

## Run the notebook

1. In your Fabric workspace, select **Import > Notebook > From this computer**, and choose
   `setup_workspace.ipynb`.
1. Open the notebook and select **Run all**. It runs on the Python or the PySpark kernel, and you don't need to
   attach a lakehouse.
1. Wait for the last code cell. The run takes about 10 to 15 minutes, mostly waiting for the service to create the
   items.

The notebook does the following, in this order:

1. **Settings**. The defaults match the tutorial. You only change them in special cases (see below).
1. **Manifest**. The list of the 28 data files (38 MB) with their checksums, and the tables with their
   row counts, columns and column types. The generator writes it from the CSV files, so it always matches the data
   on the same branch.
1. **Create the lakehouse**. Creates **TrackTraceLH** with lakehouse schemas, or uses it if it exists.
1. **Get the data**. Downloads the files from `tedescomicchidev/fabric-samples` (branch `pmi-track-and-trace-ontology`, folder
   `docs-samples/iq/ontology/new-experience`) and checks each one against its checksum.
1. **Load the lakehouse**. Uploads the CSV files to **Files**, as in part 0, and writes each table to
   **Tables > dbo**.
1. **Create and load the eventhouse**. Creates **TrackTraceEH**, creates the two tables in its KQL database, and
   loads them.
1. **Create the semantic model**. Runs the cells of `create_semantic_model.ipynb`: it creates and refreshes
   **TrackTraceKPIs** and shows the five line-days with the highest aggregation error rate. PL-02-L3 on 24 November 2026
   is at the top with 75%.
1. **Sync the SQL analytics endpoint**. Waits until the SQL analytics endpoint of the lakehouse is ready and
   syncs the new tables to it, because the ontology binds to the tables through it.
1. **Part 0 summary**. Prints the row counts.
1. **Create the ontology**. Runs the cells of `create_ontology.ipynb`, as described in
   [the shortcut for parts 1 and 2](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#run-the-notebook).

When everything works, the part 0 summary prints:

```text
Lakehouse TrackTraceLH: 18 tables under dbo with 182,829 rows, for example pack 143,842 and shipping_case 20,184.
Eventhouse TrackTraceEH: TraceEvent 182,893 rows, LineScannerTelemetry 20,736 rows.
Semantic model TrackTraceKPIs: refreshed, with the measures Packs Commissioned, Aggregation Error Rate % and Plan Attainment %.
```

And the last cell starts with:

```text
TrackTraceOntology has 22 entity types, 24 relationship types and 6 rules. Relationship bindings: mapping table.
```

Below it, the notebook prints the steps that are left in the ontology editor.

### Settings

| Setting | Default | Change it when |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE` | `"github"` | The workspace can't reach GitHub. Set `"lakehouse_files"`, see below. |
| `GITHUB_REPO`, `GITHUB_BRANCH`, `GITHUB_FOLDER` | `tedescomicchidev/fabric-samples`, `pmi-track-and-trace-ontology`, `docs-samples/iq/ontology/new-experience` | You use a fork or another branch. Use the notebook from the same branch as the data. |
| `LAKEHOUSE_FILES_SOURCE` | `setup-source` | You uploaded the sample folders to another folder under **Files**. |
| `LAKEHOUSE_NAME`, `EVENTHOUSE_NAME` | TrackTraceLH, TrackTraceEH | Rarely. The rest of the tutorial uses the defaults. |
| `CREATE_ONTOLOGY` | `True` | `False` stops after part 0, so you can build the ontology by hand in parts 1 and 2. |
| `VERIFY_CHECKSUMS` | `True` | `False` loads data files that differ from the ones the notebook was made for, for example data you changed yourself. |
| `ONTOLOGY_NAME`, `INCLUDE_OPTIONAL_RELATIONSHIPS`, `INCLUDE_INHERITED_TYPES`, `RELATIONSHIP_BINDING`, `REPLACE_EXISTING`, `SHOW_TMDL` | As in `create_ontology.ipynb` | See [the settings of the shortcut for parts 1 and 2](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#settings). |

### If the notebook can't reach GitHub

If the workspace has no internet access, the download cell stops with *Can't reach GitHub*. By then, the notebook
has created the lakehouse.

1. Download the sample folder as described in [Download sample data](tutorial-0-introduction.md#download-sample-data)
   in part 0.
1. In the lakehouse **TrackTraceLH**, create the folder **Files/setup-source**, and upload the folders `lakehouse`,
   `eventhouse` and `semantic-model` into it, with their subfolders (`lakehouse/pack` and
   `eventhouse/trace_event`).
1. In the settings cell, set `SOURCE = "lakehouse_files"`, and select **Run all** again.

### Other problems

- **"The lakehouse TrackTraceLH was created without lakehouse schemas".** The tutorial needs a lakehouse with
  schemas. Delete or rename the lakehouse, and run the notebook again.
- **"Files differ from the ones this notebook was made for".** The notebook and the data come from different
  branches or versions. Download the notebook from the branch in `GITHUB_BRANCH`. If you changed the data on
  purpose, set `VERIFY_CHECKSUMS = False`.
- **"The table ... exists with other columns".** The KQL database has a table with that name from an earlier,
  manual load with other column types. Drop it in a KQL queryset (`.drop table TraceEvent`), and run the
  notebook again.
- **"The KQL database ... isn't ready" or "The SQL analytics endpoint ... isn't ready".** New items sometimes take
  longer to provision. Run the notebook again; it reuses what it already created.
- **The ontology cells fail.** See [If the service rejects the definition](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#if-the-service-rejects-the-definition).
  Part 0 is complete at that point, so you can also set `CREATE_ONTOLOGY = False` and follow parts 1 and 2 by hand.

## Finish the ontology in the editor

Do the steps that the last cell printed. They're the same as in
[Finish the ontology in the editor](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#finish-the-ontology-in-the-editor) on the shortcut
page for parts 1 and 2: add Trace Event and Scanner Telemetry from the eventhouse, add Line Production Day with
the ontology agent, add their relationship types, and link the Scanner degradation rule. Then do
[Check the result](tutorial-1-2-shortcut.md#check-the-result).

## What's different from doing part 0 by hand

The items, names, tables and columns are the same. Some details differ:

- **Column types.** In part 0, **Load to Tables** and the eventhouse's **Get data** wizard infer the column types
  from the files. The notebook sets them explicitly from its manifest: identifiers and texts are strings, counts are integers, `requires_stamp` is a boolean, times such as `closed_ts`, `commissioned_ts` and `created_ts` are timestamps (UTC), and `commissioned_date`, `forecast_date` and `snapshot_date` are dates. In the eventhouse, the
  columns are `string`, `long`, `real` and `datetime`. The ontology cells read the types from the tables, so the
  bindings always match.
- **Empty values.** Empty fields are nulls in the lakehouse. In the eventhouse, empty numbers and times are nulls
  and empty texts are empty strings, as with the **Get data** wizard.
- **The semantic model** takes its data from the downloaded file instead of the copy embedded in
  `create_semantic_model.ipynb`. The content is the same.

## Run it again or remove it

- Running the notebook again is safe. It reuses the lakehouse and the eventhouse, replaces the lakehouse tables and
  files, loads the eventhouse tables again only if their row counts differ, and updates the semantic model.
- If **TrackTraceOntology** already has entity types, the ontology cells stop without changing it. To rebuild it, set
  `REPLACE_EXISTING = True`. That replaces its whole definition, so you need to repeat the steps in the editor.
- To remove everything, follow [Clean up resources](tutorial-7-conclusion.md#clean-up-resources) in part 7, or
  delete the items **TrackTraceOntology**, **TrackTraceKPIs**, **TrackTraceEH**, **TrackTraceLH** and the notebook.

## Next steps

After you finish the ontology in the editor, continue with [Explore the ontology](tutorial-3-explore-ontology.md).

If you set `CREATE_ONTOLOGY = False`, continue with [Create an ontology](tutorial-1-create-ontology.md) instead.
